## Goal
When provider API keys are rotated in ~/.pi/agent/auth.json, the running proxy can continue to serve stale (expired) keys indefinitely because start-proxy.sh only falls back to auth.json when an env var is unset:

    # proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh (resolve_api_keys)
    if [[ -n "${!env_var:-}" ]]; then
      echo "[env] $env_var already set from environment"
      continue
    fi

The proxy reads keys from the environment at request time (proxy/proxy/provider.py: os.environ.get(api_key_env)), so a stale env var wins over a fresh auth.json forever.

Observed failure (2026-10-18): an agent/herdr session started BEFORE a key rotation had the old keys baked into its environment; every proxy restart spawned from that session inherited them. opencode-go / -2 / -3 (endpoint https://opencode.ai/zen/go) silently served HTTP 401 api_key_expired for ~6 hours, with all traffic falling through to munitoai-free. An earlier 'test passed' was a false positive: the probe hit model=code, opencode 401'd, and the request fell through to MunitoAI which answered PONG.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: start-proxy.sh warns on startup when an api_key_env var is already set in the environment but its value differs from the key resolvable from ~/.pi/agent/auth.json for that var (fingerprint/prefix comparison is acceptable; never print full keys).
- AC2: The startup log (and/or proxy log) records a short fingerprint (e.g. first 8 chars) of each resolved provider key on every restart, so a stale-key diagnosis is possible from logs alone.
- AC3: When the env var differs from auth.json, start-proxy.sh must refuse to continue by default (fail-closed) OR require an explicit opt-out (e.g. --use-env-keys / KEEP_ENV_KEYS=1) so a rotated auth.json can never be silently ignored. Document the chosen behaviour.
- AC4: Unit tests cover: env-var-set-and-matching, env-var-set-and-differing (refuse/warn), env-var-unset (resolve from auth.json), auth.json missing.
- AC5: Full suite passes before in_review (via /skill:test).

## Notes
- Keys to cover: OPENCODE_API_KEY, OPENCODE_2_API_KEY, OPENCODE_3_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, MUNITOAI_API_KEY, MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY (any api_key_env declared in the merged config).
- discovered-from: session herdr-1792279859-3346940-27491 investigating opencode outage 2026-10-18.

# Respect MunitoAI `x-ratelimit-*` reset headers on quota 429s

## Goal

The proxy currently treats MunitoAI quota 429s as generic per-account rate
limits: it applies only the standard short provider cooldown (60s +
exponential backoff) and discards the rate-limit reset information MunitoAI
exposes via its `x-ratelimit-*` response headers. Add reset-aware handling so
an exhausted MunitoAI account is skipped with an accurate cooldown/reset time
instead of being re-tried blindly inside the reset window — while siblings on
the same gateway with independent quota (e.g. paid `munitoai` vs
`munitoai-free`) remain eligible, preserving the per-request account-key
exclusion semantics of LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N.

## Scope carve-out vs LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ (partial overlap)

- **LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ** ("honour x-ratelimit-* headers when queuing 429
  cooldowns", in-flight, Intake Complete) owns the **generic header-parsing
  engine**: parsing `x-ratelimit-reset-requests/tokens/...` and
  `x-ratelimit-over-limit` into a cooldown, behind a per-provider
  `respect_ratelimit_headers` flag (default off). It also surfaces the
  resolved cooldown in `cooldown_seconds` and provider-state.json.
- **This item** owns the **account-scoped application** on top of that
  parsing: the reset-derived cooldown must poison **only the failing account
  key** (`api_key_env`) for the remainder of the request, leaving paid
  siblings on the same gateway eligible (LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N semantics), and
  must compose correctly with the chain-hold cycle. Header parsing is a
  **blocking dependency** (LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ) — do not re-implement it in
  this item; consume the shared parse path if already merged, otherwise land
  the parser within that item first.

## Context / findings

Investigation of a live "what happens on a quota error" question (2026-10-18)
established:

- **Observed MunitoAI 429 body** (35 occurrences in proxy.log on 2026-10-18):
  `{"error":{"message":"Too Many Requests","type":"rate_limit_error","param":null,"code":"rate_limit_exceeded"}}`
  — no `Retry-After` header, no `"Resets in ..."` duration, no
  `metadata.limitName`.
- **MunitoAI signals rate-limit state via `x-ratelimit-*` headers** (live
  probe): `x-ratelimit-limit-requests`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests`,
  `x-ratelimit-reset-requests` (e.g. `"32s"`), `x-ratelimit-over-limit`.
  The proxy parses **none** of these headers (zero references in
  `proxy/proxy/*.py`).
- Because `_usage_limit_reset_info()` only recognises
  `GoUsageLimitError`/`FreeUsageLimitError` and `_parse_retry_after()` finds
  no header, `munitoai-free` gets only the standard 60s backoff cooldown and
  is re-tried every cycle — the observed logs show repeated
  `munitoai-free in cooldown (Ns remaining)` lines and fallback onto paid
  opencode/DeepSeek tiers.
- LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N (completed, v0.1.22) already makes a plain
  `rate_limit_exceeded` 429 account-keyed for *per-request eligibility* via
  `_is_account_rate_limit_error` + `_usage_limit_account_key` poisoning the
  `attempted_domains` set; this item extends reset-awareness to the
  cooldown/quarantine duration itself, consistent with that infrastructure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Reset-aware cooldown:** when a 429 `rate_limit_error` response
      from a MunitoAI provider includes an `x-ratelimit-reset-*` header
      (or `x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes` with a reset), the proxy applies the
      parsed reset duration (+ existing 2-minute safety margin) as the
      effective cooldown / quarantine for the failing account instead of the
      generic 60s backoff; a missing/zero reset value degrades to current
      behaviour.
- [ ] **AC2 — Account-scoped, sibling-preserving:** the reset-aware exclusion
      poisons only the failing account key (per `api_key_env`) for the rest
      of the request; paid siblings on the same gateway remain eligible —
      LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N semantics preserved.
- [ ] **AC3 — Fallback/chain-hold preserved:** a quota-429 account advances
      the chain to the next provider this request; chain-hold cycles
      (300s hold, max 3, 720s budget) still apply when all providers are
      exhausted.
- [ ] **AC4 — Unit tests:** (a) 429 + `x-ratelimit-reset-requests: 32s` →
      accurate cooldown, account excluded inside the reset window; (b) 429
      without any reset signal → current short-cooldown + account-key
      poisoning behaviour unchanged; (c) no regression on the
      `FreeUsageLimitError` (3h cooldown) / `GoUsageLimitError`
      (quarantine) paths.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full suite green** via `/skill:test` before `in_review`.

## Constraints

- Do not re-implement `x-ratelimit-*` header parsing — depends on the shared
  parse path from LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ.
- Keep sibling-account eligibility unchanged (LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N).

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: `_parse_retry_after()` handles only
  `Retry-After`; `_usage_limit_reset_info()` recognises only
  `GoUsageLimitError`/`FreeUsageLimitError`; `_is_account_rate_limit_error()`
  and `_usage_limit_account_key()` (from LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N) detect
  account-keyed 429s; the fallback loop applies `account_key`-scoped
  `attempted_domains` poisoning for quota 429s.

## Desired change

- On a quota 429 with a reset header, set the account's effective
  cooldown/quarantine to reset+margin (instead of 60s backoff), scoped to the
  failing `api_key_env` so siblings stay eligible; keep chain-hold and
  fallback semantics unchanged.

## Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_parse_retry_after`, `_usage_limit_reset_info`,
  `_is_account_rate_limit_error`, `_usage_limit_account_key`, cooldown
  bookkeeping and fallback loop — apply and scope the reset-derived cooldown.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — provider chain entries `munitoai` / `munitoai-free`
  (per-provider flags consumed from LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ).
- `proxy/tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` — account-key poisoning and
  sibling-eligibility tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py` — reset-path no-regression tests.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ** — "Proxy: honour MunitoAI x-ratelimit-* headers
  when queuing 429 cooldowns" (in-flight, Intake Complete) — blocking
  dependency; generic header-parsing engine.
- **LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N** — "Paid MunitoAI tier is skipped ... when the free
  tier hits a per-account 429" (completed, v0.1.22) — account-key eligibility
  foundation this item builds on.
- **LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL** — "Do not over-use MinutoAI-free" (completed) —
  free-tier request-budget gate; adjacent quota management.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q (duplicate-check, 2026-10-18): "LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ (Intake Complete,
  in-flight) already scopes honouring `x-ratelimit-*` headers for 429
  cooldowns — is this item a duplicate?" — Answer (Map): "Partial overlap,
  not a duplicate. LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ owns generic header parsing +
  provider-level cooldown; this item owns account-scoped application with
  sibling preservation (per LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N) and chain-hold interplay.
  Rewritten to carve out the delta; blocking dependency recorded." Source:
  `wl search munitoai ratelimit reset` + AC comparison of both items; comment
  added to LP-0MVDNP36J006430L.
- OPEN QUESTION — sequencing: header parsing lives in LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ,
  which is in-flight. Implementation of this item should block on that item
  (or land the parser within it first). Confirm with plan/implement stage.

# Evaluate whether `rate_limit_rpm` for `munitoai-free` should be increased

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want a measured answer to *"should `rate_limit_rpm` for
`munitoai-free` be raised above 10?"* — traded against upstream `429`s, the share
of traffic spilling to the paid `opencode` tiers, and latency — so the free tier
is used to the edge of its real allowance instead of spilling to paid capacity
for no reason (or being pushed past a limit that starts returning 429s).

## Context (current state, 2026-10-18)

- `rate_limit_rpm: 10` is declared on the three `munitoai-free` chain entries
  (`plan` / `author` / `code`) in `config.yaml` and the fast overlay — one shared
  bucket, because the limiter keys on the provider entry name (one account quota).
- `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3` → new sessions may use 7 of the 10
  slots; sessions already on the tier may use all 10 (`LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`).
- Waits are capped at 15 s, so over-budget requests now **spill** rather than
  queue. First ~4 min after that change at high demand (~19 remote dispatches/min):
  **20** free-tier vs **55** opencode dispatches (**73 % paid**), 35 new-session
  skips, 20 capped waits, 5 satisfied waits, **0** waits over 15 s.
- Upstream 429s: **0** since the 10/min gate went live. In the 12 h before the
  gate (bursts up to 72 dispatch/rolling-min) there were **19** MunitoAI
  429s (`rate_limit_exceeded`).
- Demand regularly exceeds 10/min, so some spill is arithmetically unavoidable
  at 10; the question is where the free tier's real knee sits.

## Evaluation method

1. **Establish demand** — the free-tier request rate per minute (p50/p95/max) and
   the share of minutes where demand exceeds the current budget.
2. **Find the knee** — measure upstream `429`/`rate_limit_exceeded` onset as a
   function of dispatch rate. Prefer evidence already in the logs (pre-gate
   bursts vs 429s); if a deliberate probe is needed, raise the budget
   incrementally (e.g. 10 → 12 → 15 → 20), one step per observation window
   (≥ 30 min at stable demand), and **stop at the first 429** — do not hammer a
   third-party free tier.
3. **Cost the spill** — count dispatches to `opencode`/`deepseek` attributable to
   `reason=rate_limited` / `rate_limited_after_wait` fallbacks per setting,
   expressed as a share of total remote dispatches.
4. **Latency** — confirms no regression: wait distribution stays ≤ 15 s, and
   p90/p95/p99 first-token latency for gated dispatches does not rise.
5. **Recommend** a value (keep 10 / 12 / 15 / 20 / header-derived) with the
   evidence table above; if it changes, implement it in this item with a
   documented observation window, or hand the decision to `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`
   (derive the budget from `x-ratelimit-*` headers) if a static value cannot
   track the allowance.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A measurement table of demand, upstream 429s, spill share and wait/latency per
   candidate budget (at least the current 10 plus the knee value) is attached to
   this work item as a comment.
2. The free tier's approximate 429 onset (dispatches/rolling-60 s) is established
   from log evidence, or an explicit note says why it could not be established.
3. The share of remote dispatches going to each paid tier at each candidate is
   quantified (this is the cost of a too-conservative budget).
4. A single recommendation is recorded (keep / raise to N / lower / header-derived)
   with its expected effect on 429s, paid spill and latency.
5. If a new value is adopted: it is applied to `proxy/config.yaml` **and** the fast
   overlay for all three chains, the observation window is documented, a follow-up
   check-in item is created for 24 h later, and the full project test suite passes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect any change (config comments,
   `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`).

## Constraints

- Do not remove or weaken the gate or the reserve — this item tunes one number.
- Never drive a third-party free tier into sustained 429s to "measure the limit";
  incremental, bounded steps only, one step per window.
- Any config change goes through a worktree + test/build gate; a proxy restart is
  required for it to take effect and must be noted in the measurement timeline.
- Test runs go through the test skill.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — reserve + 15 s cap (the change that made spilling the
  default over-budget behaviour).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` — the original budget gate.
- `LP-0MVDU4FDE003RQHS` — scheduled full-window effectiveness evaluation (its
  3-sub-window analysis feeds this item).
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` — header-derived (`x-ratelimit-*`) budgeting, the
  alternative to a static number.


## Key Files

- proxy/config.yaml — rate_limit_rpm: 10 on the three munitoai-free chain entries (plan / author / code).
- proxy/config-fast.yaml — the fast overlay, same three entries.
- proxy/README.md, proxy/docs/routing.md — config/routing docs to update if the value changes.
- Proxy logs (rolling 24-48 h) — demand, 429 and fallback evidence used for the measurements.

# munitoai-free rate_limit_rpm: 15 — 24h observation check-in

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want a 24-hour post-change verification that the new
`rate_limit_rpm: 15` on `munitoai-free` (raised from 10 by
LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4) does **not** drive the third-party free tier into
sustained upstream 429s, and that the predicted paid-spill reduction actually
materialises — with an explicit rollback trigger if it does not.

## Context

- LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 measured the pre-change state: at `rate_limit_rpm: 10`
  the free-tier spill was ~45 % of arrivals at peak demand (2.5 h window,
  p95 32 arrivals/min), paid (opencode.ai) share ~46 % of remote dispatches,
  upstream 429s 2 in 2.5 h (0.17 % of free dispatches). The pre-gate 429 onset
  was ≈20 dispatches/rolling-60 s (429-minute rate: 4–6 % at ≤19/min, 20 % at
  20–29, 47 % at 30–39, 100 % ≥40). The what-if simulation at capacity 15
  predicted spill ≈27 %.
- The value was changed to 15 in `proxy/config.yaml` and `proxy/config-fast.yaml`
  (all three chains: plan / author / code) with `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3`
  unchanged → new-session effective cap now **11**, affinity cap **15**.
- The change takes effect at the **next proxy restart** (T0). It was NOT
  restarted as part of LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4; the observation window starts at
  whichever restart first carries the new config. If the restart has not
  happened, this check-in must wait and re-schedule rather than measure the old
  config.
- Reproducible measurement tool: `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`
  (committed with LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4).

## Evaluation method (24 h observation window [T0, T0+24h])

1. **Restart marker:** find the first `Proxy restart attribution:` (or
   `Logging initialised at`) line in `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` after the
   LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 commit/push; that is T0. If none exists, wait (the change
   is not live).
2. **Upstream 429s:** count
   `upstream error status=429 url=https://api.munito.ai` lines in [T0, T0+24h).
   Report absolute count, per hour, and as a share of munitoai dispatches
   (`[remote] POST … -> https://api.munito.ai/inference`).
3. **Rollback trigger:** if the upstream-429 *minute* rate at peak demand
   (≥ 20 free arrivals in a rolling-60 s) exceeds ~10 % of minutes, or any
   sustained multi-minute 429 burst occurs, **revert to 10** (config + fixtures +
   tests + docs, mirroring the change in LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4) and record why.
4. **Spill confirmation:** run
   `python3 proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py` over the window and report
   the measured spill share at capacity 15 (expected ≈27 %, vs 45 % at 10) and
   the paid (opencode.ai) share of remote dispatches.
5. **Latency:** confirm waits stay ≤ 15 s (0 waits > 15 s) and MunitoAI
   first-token p90/p95/p99 does not rise vs the pre-change baseline.
6. Post the measurement table on this item (AC1-equivalent) and, when all
   rollback conditions are clear, mark it `in_review`/`completed`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The measured upstream-429 rate over [T0, T0+24h) is reported (absolute,
   per-hour, share of dispatches) with an explicit pass/fail against the
   rollback trigger.
2. The measured spill share and paid-tier share are reported and compared to
   the LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 predictions (≈27 % spill at 15).
3. Latency (wait distribution ≤ 15 s; free-tier first-token p50/p90/p95/p99) is
   reported and compared to baseline.
4. An explicit verdict is recorded: keep 15 / revert to 10 / adjust further,
   with the evidence, and the item advanced to `in_review`.
5. If the verdict is revert/adjust, the config, fixtures, tests and docs are
   updated in a worktree and the full project test suite passes (via the test
   skill).

## Constraints

- Do not restart the proxy from this session; if the config is not yet live,
  wait and re-schedule rather than measuring stale state.
- Test runs go through the test skill; never drive the free tier into sustained
  429s to probe.
- Read-only on production state except the revert path (AC5), which is its own
  approved change.
